Yes.

While it is true that if the reduced row-echelon form of a matrix has a row of zeros then that means that at least two of the equations in the system are equivalent, and that a system of two equivalent equations can have infinite solutions, this does not mean that all of the equations are equivalent. Therefore an additional non-equivalent and consistent equation could intersect the two equivalent lines at a single point. This means that the system as a whole, as long as not all of the equations are consistent and dependent, and there remains at least one consistent independent solution, then it is possible for it to have a unique solution.
